claims.text: A thin Hf interlayer on Zircaloy will form a graded Hf-Zr interface.
The graded Hf-Zr interface will promote formation of a dense, refractory HfO2 barrier during oxidation at approximately 1600 °C for 5 hours.
The Hf interlayer will significantly reduce oxidation relative to untreated Zircaloy cladding.
The Hf interlayer will reduce oxidation weight gain relative to cladding without the interlayer.
The Hf interlayer will produce a thinner oxide scale than cladding without the interlayer.
The Hf-treated cladding will retain mechanical integrity and coating adhesion in service.
A controlled sputtering or sintering process can produce a thin, continuous Hf interlayer suitable for the proposed coating architecture.
Controlling Hf-interlayer thickness will regulate interdiffusion between Hf and Zircaloy.
During high-temperature exposure, Hf will diffuse slightly into the Zircaloy substrate and create a graded interfacial layer.
Hafnium has sufficiently high oxygen affinity to form a dense HfO2 barrier under the stated conditions.
The HfO2 barrier will limit oxygen ingress into the underlying Zircaloy.
Limiting oxygen ingress will suppress further oxidation of the cladding.
Optimizing the Hf-interlayer thickness will prevent brittle-phase formation.
Preventing brittle-phase formation through thickness optimization will preserve the cladding's mechanical integrity.
Oxidation in air at approximately 1600 °C for 5 hours is representative of transient accident exposure relevant to the proposed application.
